tags.gist: Argues an evidence shift toward postmarket needs continuous, prespecified, independently verifiable monitoring, and supervisory agents held to device-grade evidence.
Commends the paper for making postmarket monitoring a first-class part of the framework rather than an afterthought.
Says relying more on postmarket monitoring works only if monitoring runs from first deployment, is prespecified and can be verified independently.
Treats the three postmarket approaches as complements, with event-driven cadence plus a calendar floor, since current PCCPs are almost all change-triggered.
Finds supervisory agents feasible and likely necessary for high-volume devices, if held to characterized error rates, independence, tamper-evidence and versioning.
Wants PCCP modification categories defined by the component changed, with re-benchmarking scope mapped to the benchmarking elements each change could affect.
Supports the shift in principle, cautioning that a discontinuous, retrospective or unverifiable postmarket record deletes the evidence burden rather than moving it.
Wants monitoring continuous from day one of deployment and linked to the premarket baseline, since a later-started program has no baseline.
Wants analyses, thresholds, sampling frames, cadence and triggers fixed before deployment, applying the premarket prespecification principle to monitoring.
Wants monitoring records independently verifiable: append-only, timestamped and under Part 11-like controls, not dependent on sponsor attestation.
Wants a prespecified consequence pathway for threshold breaches, such as escalation, rollback or FDA notification, so breaches are not negotiations.
Would exclude functions high on both risk axes and devices whose failures are undetectable in deployment data, making detectability an eligibility criterion.
Reports a review of 95 authorized PCCPs: postmarket evaluation is almost entirely change-triggered, with one cadence and one quantified trigger found.
Urges treating re-benchmarking, clinician review and degradation monitoring as layers of one program, since each has a distinct blind spot.
Wants event-driven reassessment triggered by input shifts, component changes and volume milestones, with a prespecified maximum interval as floor.
Says supervisory agents are feasible and probably the only scalable coverage for high-volume open-ended devices, complementing review and re-benchmarking.
Wants the supervisor validated against independent human adjudication, with prespecified sensitivity and specificity re-confirmed periodically on fresh samples.
Flags correlated failure when supervisor and device share a model class; suggests vendor diversity, challenge sets and targeted human calibration.
Wants the adjudicator independence expectation extended to supervisors, with judgment independent of sponsor objectives and append-only logged outputs.
Wants supervisor updates documented as monitoring-program modifications, with material changes re-validated against human adjudication.
Suggests qualifying supervisory monitoring methods through MDDT or similar, so each submission need not relitigate the monitor.
Reports that authorized PCCP categories center on retraining and locked model artifacts, with none covering prompt, retrieval, guardrail or model-version changes.
Says GenAI behavior changes through prompts, corpora, guardrails or upstream model versions without retraining, so a taxonomy lacking those categories fails.
Proposes PCCP categories by component changed, each mapped in advance to the benchmarking elements it could affect; model version changes trigger full re-benchmarking.
Wants the re-benchmarking baseline versioned, with pinned datasets and adjudicators, and granular to element and subgroup level.
Says platforms change models silently on their own schedules; suggests CDRH judge sponsors on a layered stack of mechanisms.
Calls contractual notification a necessary floor but insufficient, since notices describe intent rather than effects on a specific device.
Calls version pinning the strongest single mitigation, though not always offered, eventually retired, and blind to changes beneath a stable label.
Proposes a fixed, versioned canary set run on a cadence against a stored baseline to detect unannounced upstream model changes.
Treats continuous degradation monitoring as the backstop, since a time-correlated shift across deployments signals an upstream change.
Wants a detected third-party change to carry the same evidence obligation under the PCCP as a sponsor-chosen change of that scope.
Concludes the evidence shift is sound only with continuous, prespecified, verifiable monitoring, and urges making these practices the norm for AI devices generally.
Concludes supervisory agents must serve as the coverage layer only if held to characterized error rates, independence, tamper-evidence and version control.
